title: Move traffic without turning an incident into a rewrite
description: Switch rollout states to trace the old and new paths, the evidence used for promotion, and the rollback behavior when the candidate fails.

nodes.label: Shopper
nodes.detail: Sends a checkout request. A cohort rule keeps the customer on one implementation for the duration of the request and its follow-up work.

nodes.label: Migration router
nodes.detail: Routes eligible traffic to the candidate, retains a fast switch back to the monolith, and records which version served each request.

nodes.label: Monolith path
nodes.detail: Remains available while migration evidence is incomplete. It is a rollback target, not a second permanent write owner for the same fact.

nodes.label: Fulfillment candidate
nodes.detail: Serves a bounded cohort with deadlines, idempotency, a compatible data contract, and a declared fallback behavior.

nodes.label: Inventory store
nodes.detail: Records stock and reservations for the candidate. Its saturation and reservation outcomes are rollout guardrails, not just infrastructure details.

nodes.label: Comparison telemetry
nodes.detail: Receives versioned latency, errors, fallback volume, and result comparison data without delaying a customer request.

nodes.label: Rollout controller
nodes.detail: Applies a declared observation window and guardrails. It pauses promotion or restores the previous path when evidence is missing or unhealthy.

scenarios.label: Shadow compare
scenarios.summary: The monolith serves the customer response while the candidate processes an eligible read or dry-run command. Results are compared asynchronously before any customer is moved.
scenarios.result: Comparison exposes semantic differences early. A mismatch is a boundary or contract problem to fix before canary traffic, not a reason to add more retries.

scenarios.label: Healthy canary
scenarios.summary: A small cohort reaches the candidate. Its domain result, latency, error rate, and inventory saturation remain within the promotion policy for the observation window.
scenarios.result: Promotion may continue only after evidence is healthy. Keep the prior path compatible and the cohort versioned so a rollback is immediate and explainable.

scenarios.label: Inventory timeout
scenarios.summary: The candidate reaches its inventory deadline. The router stops increasing the cohort while the controller records the breach and sends new eligible requests back to the prior path.
scenarios.result: Rollback protects new requests first. Reconcile in-flight reservations using their idempotency keys and event history; do not retry indefinitely against an already saturated store.

scenarios.label: Missing evidence
scenarios.summary: The candidate still answers requests, but comparison telemetry is unavailable. The team has lost the proof needed to expand the cohort safely.
scenarios.result: Freeze promotion or restore the previous path. Serving traffic is not sufficient evidence that correctness, saturation, and customer outcomes remain healthy.
